security_audit.summary: All static command-execution and reconnaissance alerts were false positives from Markdown SQL examples, inline SQL function names, and database indexing terminology. I found no prompt-injection text, data-exfiltration intent, or real shell execution. The only semantic issue is overbroad Write permission in SKILL.md for a read-only SQL reference skill.

remediation.issue: The skill grants Write tool access even though it is a read-only SQL reference.
remediation.suggestion: Change allowed-tools to Read unless a documented editing workflow is added.

content.value_statement: SQL teams often need reliable examples for common query patterns and performance decisions. This skill provides concise references for CTEs, window functions, joins, pagination, and indexes.
actual_capabilities: Shows CTE examples, including chained CTEs for staged aggregation.
Summarizes core window functions such as ROW_NUMBER, LAG, LEAD, SUM OVER, and AVG OVER.
Compares common JOIN types and when their row sets differ.
Provides offset and keyset pagination examples for product queries.
Explains B-tree, hash, GIN, GiST, composite, covering, partial, and expression indexes.
Lists common SQL anti-patterns with safer query alternatives.
limitations: It does not connect to databases or inspect live schemas.
Examples are generic and may need syntax changes for each SQL engine.
It does not benchmark query plans or measure production performance.
It does not validate security controls such as row-level access policies.

use_cases.title: Design analytical queries
use_cases.description: Build rankings, running totals, session detection, and deduplication with window function examples.

use_cases.title: Review application SQL
use_cases.description: Compare joins, pagination choices, and anti-pattern fixes during code review.

use_cases.title: Plan index changes
use_cases.description: Choose index types and column order before proposing database migrations.

prompt_templates.title: Find a basic pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sql-patterns skill to show a simple CTE pattern for filtering active users. Explain when to use it.

prompt_templates.title: Compare query choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sql-patterns skill to compare offset pagination and keyset pagination for a product list.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an analytical query
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sql-patterns skill to suggest window function patterns for ranking, running totals, and deduplication in a sales report.

prompt_templates.title: Plan indexing strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sql-patterns skill to review a query with filters, sorting, and joins. Recommend index types and column order.

output_examples.input: I need the latest order per user without duplicate rows.
output_examples.output: A response explains row-number deduplication, partitioning by user, sorting by update time, and filtering to the first row.

output_examples.input: My product list uses high offset pagination and is slow.
output_examples.output: A response compares offset pagination with keyset pagination and recommends a stable sort column for large result sets.

output_examples.input: Which index helps filters on status and created date?
output_examples.output: A response discusses selectivity, equality filters, range filters, and composite index column order.

best_practices: Share the database engine and version before asking for syntax guidance.
Include table sizes, filter columns, sort columns, and join keys when requesting index advice.
Ask for tradeoffs when choosing between readability, portability, and performance.
anti_patterns: Treating the examples as production-ready without adapting names, types, and constraints.
Requesting index advice without sharing the query shape or expected cardinality.
Using SELECT star in examples that need stable, reviewed column lists.

faq.question: Does this skill run SQL queries?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference patterns and explanations. It does not connect to a database.

faq.question: Which SQL engines are covered?
faq.answer: The examples focus on common SQL concepts and include PostgreSQL-style indexing notes.

faq.question: Can it help with performance reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can point to indexing, pagination, and anti-pattern checks for human review.

faq.question: Can it replace a database expert?
faq.answer: No. It supports analysis but cannot inspect workload, data distribution, or production constraints.

faq.question: Does it include window function examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers ranking, navigation functions, running totals, session detection, and deduplication.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it in repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code and Codex can use the references while reviewing SQL files.
